gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long a replacement DVR can record before it overwrites. Using the inputs on Dahua's own page (2 SATA bays at up to 16 TB each, video up to 8,192 kbps per channel), the XVR7208A-4K-I3 holds about 45 days of 24/7 footage from 8 coax cameras even with every channel at maximum bitrate. The $99.99 ANNKE DR88 tops out at one 8 TB drive, or 1 TB per BNC camera.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rivals. The Dahua XVR7208A-4K-I3 product page lists the raw inputs (2 HDD × 16 TB, 32–8,192 kbps, 8 BNC) but gives no recording-duration estimate. The Hikvision DS-7208HQHI-S1/XT page returned no content when I fetched it, and the Hikvision datasheet PDF wasn't readable. ChatGPT's other results are Dahua datasheets and catalog pages with no prices, so none of them states a price per camera input or days of retention. ChatGPT's answer says 'SATA hard-drive support for continuous local recording' but never puts a number on it.
decides: Retention per camera separates the budget picks from the step-up picks. The DR88 ($12.50 per BNC input) and ZOSI ZR08VMA ($8.75 per BNC input) are cheapest per camera. The DR88 has only one bay, capped at 8 TB, so it gives 1 TB per camera. The Viewtron VT-DVR-8 (2 × 12 TB = 3 TB per BNC camera, $100 per BNC input) and the Dahua XVR7208A-4K-I3 (32 TB = 4 TB per BNC camera) are for shoppers who need weeks of continuous recording at high bitrate. This confirms the DR88 as the value pick for typical home retention. Anyone who needs about 45 days of footage at full bitrate should step up to a 2-bay unit.
